DILG BAGONG PLIP'NAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor- Quezon Avenue, west Triangle, Quezon City SEP 12 2025 www.dilq.qov.ph OPINION NO Ita- DR. KYRIACOS LOUCA JR., DPA kyriacosloucajr@gmail.com Dear Dr. Kyriacos Louca Jr.: EP 025 This refers to your electronic communication dated 03 July2025s ng clarifi on whether a Local Chief Executive or any officer Of a Local Governme I (LGU) may lawfully interfere in the resolution and decisions of a senior citizens' organization—particularly as to when and how the elections of its officers shall be conducted—considering that the right to self-organization is a constitutional right. At the outset, allow us to affirm that the right to self-organization is indeed guaranteed under the 1987 Philippine Constitution, specifically under Article III, Section 8, which provides: "The right of the people, including those employed in the public and private sectors, to form unions, associations, or societies for purposes not contrary to law shall not be abridged." This constitutional guarantee encompasses the autonomy of duly constituted non- governmental, non-profit, and private organizations—such as senior citizens' organizations—to govern their internal affairs, including the manner and timing of their elections, provided such conduct is not inconsistent with their by-laws, enabling charters, or relevant laws and regulations. Consistent with this, and as earlier opined by the Department in DILG Opinion No. 125, s. 2024, senior citizens' organizations that are duly registered and/or recognized— whether with the National Commission of Senior Citizens (NCSC), the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the Cooperative Development Authority (CDA), or other competent regulatory bodies—are deemed independent and autonomous entities. Furthermore, the Local Government Code of 1991 (Republic Act No. 7160), particularly Sections 34 to 36, underscores the limited role of LGUs in relation to people's and non- governmental organizations. While LGUs are encouraged to forge partnerships and extend support (financial or otherwise) to such organizations for purposes of service delivery and local development, they are not authorized to control or dictate their internal processes, including electoral matters. In view of the foregoing, this Department reiterates that Local Government Units have no legal authority to interfere, dictate, or coerce any senior citizens' organization with respect to *the conduct of its elections. Any action by an LGU official that unjustly intrudes upon the internal affairs of such organizations may be construed as a violation "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 887644-54

of the constitutional right to self-organization and may be subject to appropriate administrative or legal remedies. The opinion of this Department is rendered solely based on the facts presented and our understanding thereof. We trust that this clarifies the matter and affirms the constitutional and statutory protections granted to the organizations concerned. Very truly yours, ATTY. ROMEO P. BENITEZ Undersecretary foc External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELLA/RPB/LLLS-LRALLD/jjmm Page 2 of 2
